column1: ! phrasing. A subset: one case per ender chord, then a prime stride through the
! ender table and through the clause dimensions, so the sample cycles every
! setting rather than landing on one corner of each. The whole language is 128
! subject sets times the clause dimensions times 668 enders, which no file holds.
! The expectations are this grammar's own answers, recorded when phrasing.py was
! still the oracle and agreed with them. A line that changes here is a change to
! what a clause writes: read it, then update it.
! A line with no tab claims the stroke has no entry. 562 do, and nearly all of
! them are the dropped coordinate subjects: the file asserts the drop rather than
! ignoring it. The others are a modifier stroke, a passive with no verb, and a
! determiner subject under a second hole.

column1: ! The hole ender, `-rg`: the verb of the clause is the word written next, so the
! record ends in the tail that asks for its form. Every corner of the clause
! grammar still applies, which is the whole point of putting it here rather than
! in a dictionary of phrases: agreement, aspect, modality, the passive, the
! question and do-support all read the same as they do with a verb of their own.
! A base form asks for nothing, because the word as written is the base form.
! The three below it are what the hole displaced: bare `hear` at `-rgt`, `hear
! about` at `-rpgt`, and `never hear` where it always was.
! The adverb enders, which all carry the hole: an adverb inflects for nothing, so
! a clause ending on one has no verb for its tense or aspect to inflect either.
! `-d` is therefore the tense it is everywhere else, which is a past the launchpad
! never had, and do-support fires only for the negative and the question, as it
! does for a verb of its own.
! ---- the determiner subjects (§4.1f), whose noun is the word written next.
! Both exclusions are here as no-entry rows: an adverb ender and a `-RG` verb
! are holes of their own, and one record waits for one unit.
